initiative.title: Block-based note storage
initiative.summary: Replace dual html/markdown note storage with canonical TipTap JSON blocks (stable IDs) plus derived block/link indexes, enabling links+backlinks, inline TaskItems, fixed cross-note views, and block-level AI/MCP edits; remove bulk ingest.
initiative.next_action: User: review/merge the stack, deploy, run Admin > Migrations dry run then convert on prod; m9 (drop legacy columns) after soak

claims.statement: Dual html/markdown storage is a mess: markdown goes stale after first editor save, readers guess which is current, conversions lossy.
Move to a block system as the single canonical storage format for in-app creation and edits.
Focus exclusively on in-app generation and edits; no bulk ingest for a while.
Remove bulk ingest (cli-ingest, POST /api/docs ingest) now.
First release unlocks: note/block links, typed inline objects, cross-note queries, precise AI/MCP block edits.
Blocks have stable IDs and live in exactly one note; moving keeps ID; no transclusion.
Convert all existing notes once; small loss OK; old HTML kept as backup.
Links + backlinks is the first proof.
First typed inline object is tasks only.
AI/MCP sees markdown annotated with block IDs and edits by block ID; blocks stay canonical.
Concurrency: per-block merge; same-block conflict newer wins, other saved as revision; no live cursors.
Appetite: implemented in one night as stacked PRs, all capabilities.
Inline checkbox creates a real TaskItem synced with Tasks.
Cross-note queries are fixed views (backlinks, open tasks, #tag), no query language.
Keep html/markdown columns briefly during migration; then keep only a derived text/markdown form if it helps embeddings perf; ideal is blocks only with a text field per block.
ChatGPT MCP write path uses originalSource/originalContentId for idempotency; those columns must survive ingest removal.
sanitize-html allowlist strips unknown attributes, blocking richer node types.
Time blocks, archived pages, data tables (PRD) as later block types.
In-app editing experience must be top notch (autosave, revisions, safety).
New inline tasks go into a single Inbox task list.

conflicts.summary: Remove ingest vs ChatGPT connector reusing ingest identity columns
conflicts.resolution: Remove ingest code paths; keep originalSource/originalContentId columns for MCP idempotency.

shape.appetite: One night, stacked PRs; each PR leaves the app shippable; legacy column drop is a later PR after soak.
shape.problem: Notes have no trustworthy canonical format and no addressable sub-units, blocking links, typed objects, queries, and precise AI edits.
shape.recommended_shape: Canonical TipTap JSON per note (Doc.content + contentVersion) with stable block ids via @tiptap/extension-unique-id; one UI-free shared schema module used by editor, server (static-renderer, markdown, html) and migration; derived DocBlock and DocLink tables rebuilt in the save transaction; per-block 3-way merge using base version + revision snapshots; MCP markdown with ^block-id annotations and id-targeted ops; taskRef node bound to TaskItem; fixed views over DocBlock/DocLink; ingest removed first; legacy html/markdown dual-written behind a read switch until cutover.

rejected_alternatives.name: Row-per-block canonical storage
rejected_alternatives.reason: Requires reassembly on every read and hand-maintained parent/order invariants for nested lists/tables without making any of the four target features easier; derived rows keyed by block id deliver the same query/link/merge power.

rejected_alternatives.name: Freeze legacy columns at migration
rejected_alternatives.reason: Loses a true rollback; dual-write via static renderer/markdown serializer is cheap and keeps share/search/embeddings readable until each reader is switched.

rejected_alternatives.name: Real-time CRDT (Yjs)
rejected_alternatives.reason: User chose per-block merge; single user, no presence needed.

success_moves.risk_reduced: Fewer writers/readers to keep compatible during migration.

success_moves.move: UI-free shared schema module consumed by client and server
success_moves.risk_reduced: Schema drift between editor and server; NodeView imports breaking server build.

success_moves.move: Dry-run migration against local DB copy with per-note text-loss report
success_moves.risk_reduced: Silent content loss in one-time conversion.

success_moves.move: Dual-write legacy columns behind a read switch
success_moves.risk_reduced: No rollback if a reader breaks after cutover.

success_moves.move: Pure merge function (base, mine, theirs by block id) unit-tested before wiring to editor
success_moves.risk_reduced: Concurrency bugs only discoverable in live multi-tab use.

success_moves.move: Block-ID stability test: 3 edit/save/reload cycles + cross-note paste + duplicate-id paste
success_moves.risk_reduced: Links and tasks built on churning IDs.

first_proof.question: Do block IDs survive real edits and does migration preserve existing notes well enough to build on?
first_proof.artifact: Shared schema + content column + migration dry-run report on local copy of real notes, plus [[ links and backlinks
first_proof.observation: Converted count and notes with >2% text loss; IDs stable across 3 save/reload cycles and cross-note paste; backlink appears within one save
first_proof.decision_rule: If IDs churn or more than a handful of notes lose meaningful content, fix schema/ID strategy before stacking tasks, merge, or MCP

rabbit_holes.risk: Applying a server-merged document into a live editor without cursor jumps
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Apply only changed blocks by id as a ProseMirror transaction; fallback: defer apply until editor blur and show 'updated elsewhere'.

rabbit_holes.risk: Server-side HTML parsing (@tiptap/html generateJSON) needs a DOM shim in Node
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Use @tiptap/html server entry (bundled DOM); run migration as a script, not request path.

rabbit_holes.risk: Custom nodes (code block lowlight, image width, tables, emoji) not round-tripping through markdown
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Markdown is interchange only; JSON canonical; fixture tests per node type.

rabbit_holes.risk: TaskItem <-> taskRef sync loops and orphan handling
rabbit_holes.mitigation: TaskItem is the source of task state; node stores only taskId; deletion detaches rather than deletes.
Derive sections from DocBlock text grouped by heading blocks.
